Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: realtime chat summaries and contextual assistant inside FintechAI dashboard.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~50M tokens/month (with bursts up to 80M).
- Average request size: ~150 tokens (prompt+response).
- SLA target: p50 ~150-200ms, p95 target around 400-500ms for UI interactions.
- Budget range you mentioned: $10k–$15k/month to start.

Open questions I captured:
1) Target unit economics: do you have a hard target $/1M tokens (you mentioned ~ $20/1M as a direction on the call)?
2) Are you open to a POC on Dedicated vs Hosted to measure latency with your prompts?
3) Any procurement constraints/timing from your side (PO, vendor forms)?

How Redwood can help / immediate recommendations:
- For p50 ~150ms with 150-token average, our Hosted Premium tier with streaming + small-batch config typically hits that on the models we benchmark for convo-style workloads.
- If you want stronger p95 guarantees, Dedicated with reserved capacity and aggressive batching controls is the best ROI — gives consistent latency and lower per-token unit cost at scale.
- Streaming improves perceived latency (tokens stream to client) but does not reduce total token consumption; batching reduces cost but can increase tail latency.

Attached: redwood_pricing_v3.xlsx (ballpark unit costs + example math for 50M tokens) and SLA-latency-tiers.pdf (explain tradeoffs and suggested configs).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm target $/1M token goal (helps me build two concrete SKU options).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Vivek to run your sample prompts (30–45m).
- If procurement is ready, loop in Procurement and we’ll share a mutual action plan / 30-day POC scope.

I’ve tentatively proposed two time options for the deep-dive — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget and target unit cost:
- $10k–$15k/month is our initial procurement band. Our spreadsheet owner wants to see unit economics expressed as $/1M tokens. Goal for year 1 is sub-$25/1M tokens; ideally hitting ~$18–$22/1M at scale.

2) Volumes and traffic shape:
- Baseline 50M tokens/month, expected growth to ~120M over 12 months if engagement hits target.
- Peak concurrency: up to ~120 RPS during market open hours (lots of short chats).
- Token distribution skewed: many short messages (~40–80 tokens) and some long summarizations (~400–800 tokens).

3) Latency priorities:
- UX team prioritizes perceived latency (first token delivered) -> p50 matters most, p95 is nice but not mandatory for MVP.
- Open to streaming to improve perceived latency even if total end-to-end time is similar.

4) Procurement timeline:
- We can start a 30-day eval in Sept; procurement can turn quickly if we have clear pricing and a short POC SOW.

Can you send two ballpark options: Hosted (with expected $/1M and expected p50/p95) and Dedicated (with committed volume tiers and preferred batch/stream configs and $/1M)? Also include expected unit cost sensitivity as we move from 50M->120M tokens.

—Alex

Alex — thanks, this is very helpful. Below are two concrete, ballpark options (high level) that I’ll also capture in an updated spreadsheet and send after the deep-dive. Numbers are illustrative — final depends on exact prompt mix, concurrency, and chosen model/quantization.

Option A — Hosted Premium (fast start, no infra commitment):
- Expected unit cost (50M tokens): ~$24/1M tokens
- Expected unit cost (120M tokens): ~$20/1M tokens (volume discount tiers applied)
- Latency: p50 ~120–200ms with streaming enabled; p95 typically 350–600ms depending on prompt length.
- Config: streaming + small-batch (batch window 10–20ms) to preserve p50.
- Pros/cons: Fast onboarding, no contract, slightly higher unit cost at scale; good for validating product fit.

Option B — Dedicated Reserved Capacity (best unit economics and stable tail latency):
- Commit tiers: 50M/mo, 100M/mo, 200M/mo (we can size a pool based on 50–120M baseline).
- Expected unit cost (50M commit): ~$16–18/1M tokens
- Expected unit cost (120M commit): ~$12–15/1M tokens
- Latency: p50 ~80–160ms; p95 can be driven down with aggressive routing and reserved pool to ~250–400ms.
- Config: dedicated GPUs, controlled batching (workload-aware batching with KV cache warm-ups), optional streaming for perceived latency.
- Pros/cons: Lower unit cost, stronger SLOs, procurement/commitment required.

Notes on batching vs streaming tradeoffs:
- Batching (larger batch windows) increases throughput and reduces cost but increases tail latency. We can tune batch window per route; for UI routes we keep window small and enable streaming.
- Streaming helps perceived latency by returning tokens early — minimal impact on cost, slight CPU/network overhead for chunked responses.
- SLO-driven pricing: we can model a blended price that accounts for reserved capacity + premium for stricter p95 guarantees if you want contractual SLOs.

Recommended next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek — we’ll bring a profiling harness to run a sample of 1000 representative prompts and report p50/p95 and throughput. (30–45m)
2) I’ll update the spreadsheet with exact math for 50M vs 120M and two SKU proposals (Hosted and Dedicated).
3) If procurement is ready, we’ll draft a 30-day POC SOW (scope + success metrics).

I’ll attach the updated pricing sheet in a follow-up after the deep-dive. Proposed deep-dive times: Tue 9/2 10:00am PT or Wed 9/3 11:00am PT. Which works?

Thanks — Marissa
